images.title: The ant on the grid
images.purpose: Show a distance and a direction on a grid of 1 cm squares: a leaf 4 cm to the west, a seed 6 cm to the south, and a berry that needs two legs, 2 cm to the east and then 4 cm to the north, 6 cm in all.
images.composition: A tall grid on the left with the anthill and the ant near its middle and three foods on its edges, each reached by a coloured arrow with a length pill; a panel on the right that says each path in words, a compass card and the key that one square is 1 cm.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. At the top, centred at x 728 and y 45, the title The ant on the grid in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (44 px). THE GRID: one grid of 7 columns by 10 rows of equal squares, every square 64 by 64 px, so the grid is 448 px wide and 640 px tall and holds exactly 70 squares; it covers x 160 to 608 and y 100 to 740; thin grey #6B7280 grid lines (2 px) and a 3 px dark #2B2B2B outline. No numbers are written on the grid. THE ANTHILL AND THE ANT: the anthill point is the grid point at x 416, y 356 (4 squares from the left edge and 4 squares from the top edge). A grey #6B7280 mound, a half ellipse 60 px wide and 26 px high, sits with its flat base on the horizontal grid line through that point, centred on x 416. On top of the mound stands one small ant drawn from 3 touching dark #1F2937 circles in a row (rear 16 px, middle 12 px, head 12 px) with 6 thin dark legs, about 44 px wide, centred at x 416, y 326. THE THREE FOODS, each on a grid point: one green #009E73 leaf, an ellipse 60 px by 34 px tilted a little, centred at x 160, y 356 (4 squares to the west of the anthill point, on the left edge of the grid); one seed, a dark #1F2937 ellipse 24 px wide and 36 px high, centred at x 416, y 740 (6 squares to the south of the anthill point, on the bottom edge of the grid); one berry, a vermilion #D55E00 circle 40 px across with a small white highlight, centred at x 544, y 100 (the berry is 2 squares to the east and then 4 squares to the north of the anthill point, on the top edge of the grid). THE FOUR PATH PARTS, each a thick arrow (8 px line, 26 px arrowhead at the far end, pointing away from the anthill point): (1) a teal #0072B2 arrow from x 416 to x 160 at y 356, 4 squares long, pointing west to the leaf; (2) an amber #E69F00 arrow from y 356 to y 740 at x 416, 6 squares long, pointing south to the seed; (3) a reddish purple #CC79A7 arrow from x 416 to x 544 at y 356, 2 squares long, pointing east, and (4) a reddish purple #CC79A7 arrow from y 356 to y 100 at x 544, 4 squares long, pointing north to the berry (arrows 3 and 4 meet at the grid point x 544, y 356, where the path turns). FOUR LENGTH PILLS, each a white rounded rectangle 76 by 40 px with a 3 px outline in its arrow's colour and the text in dark bold 28 px: 4 cm centred at x 288, y 326 (above the teal arrow); 6 cm centred at x 470, y 548 (to the right of the amber arrow); 2 cm centred at x 480, y 386 (below the east part of the reddish purple path); 4 cm centred at x 596, y 228 (to the right of the north part of the reddish purple path). NAME LABELS (dark bold 26 px): ant centred at x 416, y 290 (above the ant); anthill right aligned to end at x 400, y 392 (below the teal arrow, left of the anthill point); leaf centred at x 160, y 400; seed centred at x 416, y 782; berry left aligned from x 574, y 100. THE RIGHT PANEL, x 700 to 1400: three white rounded rectangles with a 3 px dark #2B2B2B outline, each with a coloured bar 16 px wide on its left edge; box 1 at y 190 to 290 with a teal bar holds the text Leaf: 4 cm towards the west; box 2 at y 320 to 420 with an amber bar holds the text Seed: 6 cm towards the south; box 3 at y 450 to 600 with a reddish purple bar holds the text Berry: 2 cm towards the east, then 4 cm towards the north, wrapped on two lines after the comma, and below it, on a third line, the text 2 + 4 = 6 cm in all in bold; all text in these boxes is dark #1F2937 32 px, left aligned from x 740. COMPASS: a compass card, a square 120 by 120 px at x 1280 to 1400 and y 30 to 150, white with a #2B2B2B outline (3 px), with N at the top (centred at x 1340, y 56), S at the bottom (x 1340, y 124), W at the left (x 1306, y 90) and E at the right in red #D55E00 (x 1374, y 90), all bold 26 px, placed at the top right. SQUARE KEY: at x 700 to 732 and y 676 to 708 a white square with a thin dark outline and a small double arrow across it, and to its right, left aligned from x 750 at y 692, the text 1 square = 1 cm in dark 30 px. In all: 1 grid of 70 squares, 1 mound, 1 ant, 3 foods, 4 arrows, 4 pills, 3 panel boxes, 1 compass card. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: Count the squares along a grid line for the distance, say the direction, and write a path with a turn as one leg after another: 2 cm towards the east, then 4 cm towards the north is 2 + 4 = 6 cm.
images.description: A grid of 1 cm squares with an ant at its anthill, a leaf 4 cm to the west, a seed 6 cm to the south and a berry reached by 2 cm to the east and then 4 cm to the north.
images.context: Concept image for Distance and Direction on a Grid. It follows the idea of the ant's grid in your maths book (squares of 1 cm, a compass, an ant crawling along the grid lines) and uses the numbers of this concept's own example, not the numbers of the book's questions.
images.teaching_notes: Count the squares of each arrow aloud with the child, then say the leg as a distance and a direction. The slip to watch: reading a distance without its direction, or counting the corner square twice on the path with a turn.

image_decisions.why: The squares of the grid make a distance countable and a path with a turn visible as two legs, which words alone do not.
